description: Notarize-only contract for durable Agent Work Context. A registered agent is a durable identity; the sessions that do its work (any model, any harness) are ephemeral. Each record of this type is an immutable, signed checkpoint of the state of a piece of work, so a new session holding the agent's key resumes without the prior conversation. Pattern: ONE root record represents the work; every checkpoint is a CHILD of that root via parentRecordId (checkpoints are siblings, never children of each other) and SUPERSEDES the checkpoint it replaces via the top-level supersedesRecordId field on POST /v1/records. supersedesRecordId is a first-class record field, NOT a criteria field: the engine validates that the target exists in your org, refuses the create with 404 when it does not, and indexes the relation. FIND THE CURRENT STATE with one call: GET /v1/records/search?parentRecordId=<rootId>&type=work-context-v1&superseded=false returns the live head. It returns more than one row only when sessions forked, which is the honest answer rather than a guess. The first checkpoint uses checkpointReason 'initial' and supersedes nothing; every later checkpoint sets supersedesRecordId to the id of the head it replaces, and forgetting to means the old head stays current too, so the omission surfaces as two current heads instead of passing silently. Resume by reading the head's resumeInstructions and pendingWork (first entry = next action), then write your own checkpoint under the same root superseding the head. Large artifacts belong in references entries (system/refType/refId, digest in attributes), not inline; criteria is capped at 10KB, so keep completedWork summarized rather than unbounded.

objective.description: What this work is trying to achieve, stated durably: it should read correctly at every checkpoint from first to last.

summary.description: Current state of the work in plain language. This is the first thing a cold-start agent reads; write it for a reader with zero prior conversation.

acceptanceCriteria.description: What good looks like: the conditions under which this work is done. If the work is gated, these should mirror the criteria on the gated record that will render the verdict.

completedWork.description: Work finished as of this checkpoint, kept to the RECENT working set. Do not carry the full history forward: superseded checkpoints remain on-chain, so the supersedes chain is the archive. Summarize older progress in `summary`. When an entry refers to a record this work created, include that record's id so the claim is checkable.

pendingWork.description: Work remaining, ordered. The first entry is what the resuming agent should do next.

decidedBy.description: Who rendered the decision: a human principal, a system of record, or an agent id.

decisions.description: Decisions made so far, with rationale. A resuming agent honors these; reopening one is itself a decision worth recording.

assumptions.description: What the work currently assumes true but has not confirmed. A resuming agent treats these as unverified.

constraints.description: Boundaries the work must respect (budget, scope, policy, technical). Durable across checkpoints unless a recorded decision changes them.

openQuestions.description: Unresolved questions blocking or shaping the work, including who can answer each if known.

uri.description: Where the evidence lives, if externally addressable.

evidence.description: Evidence gathered so far that supports the work's conclusions. Point at sources; do not inline large content.

checkpointReason.description: Why this checkpoint was written. `initial` is the first checkpoint under a root and the only one that supersedes nothing; every later checkpoint sets the top-level `supersedesRecordId` on the create call (a record field, not a criteria field). `handoff` signals a different session is expected to resume; `final` marks the work complete (pendingWork must be empty).

resumeInstructions.description: Direct instructions to whoever resumes: what to do first, what to read, what not to redo. The single highest-value field for a cold start; write it every checkpoint.
